comment_data.body:
Looking at the call sites to FullName_save(), the logic changes in many places if FullName_save() returns NULL. We probably don't want that. 

On line 421 the FAIL result means `vim_FullName()` truncated the string. But then in the `else` branch we just blindly copy the string without truncating it. ~~Instead we should truncate it.~~

We can't return NULL for failure, for reason mentioned in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/5737#discussion_r91745980. Some call sites _expect_ the full, un-expanded path to be returned. 

We could examine all the calls to FullName_save(), but that could be a big refactor project, and would entail replacing `FullName_save()` with a new function so that we don't get confused when merging patches from Vim.
No. `retval=FAIL` if `path_get_absolute_path()` returns `FAIL`. With your changes the behavior has changed.
The uppercase variants of the various string functions are "legacy". Prefer `xfoo` if it's possible to do so without a cast.
if this fails it should truncate, as before
making this `} else if (path_get...) {` saves a level of indentation and helps readability
It returns early if `fname` needs to be truncated at [L1665](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/5737/files#diff-d2b13f507f185cdf05782bb8265bc7c4R1665)
`path_get_absolute_path()` may fail for other reasons. E.g. `append_path()` could grow the result beyond `len`. We must keep the behavior the same as before, unless there is a reason to change it.

No it can't, that would be a heap overflow. If it returns `FAIL` then it's guaranteed to only copy `fname`.

The result is the same as before.

What was _gained_ by changing `xstrlcpy(buf, fname, len);` to `strcpy(buf, fname);`, in that case? We changed the logic, for no reason. Now one must scrutinize the (numerous) failure modes of `path_get_absolute_path()` to make sure this logic change is ok; and any possible upstream Vim changes to `vim_FullName()` must be reconciled with these changes.
I noticed that the linter also complained about using `strcpy`. `xstrlcpy` is safer, so sure.
There are now 3 paths in this function that return `xstrlcpy(buf, fname, len);`. Seems like the old approach of assigning a `retval` saves duplication, and is arguably clearer.

The branches do completely different things, which makes this much more readable:

1. Truncates too long path and returns `FAIL`
2. Copies URL and returns `OK`
3. Copies absolute path and returns `OK`
4. Copies path and returns `FAIL`

The compiler can easily optimize this.

I didn't mention optimization. But they all do the same thing: `xstrlcpy(buf, fname, len);`. Only they return a different value.

The general idea is that if there's not a clear advantage to making a formatting change, then leaving it alone is better than not. Reason I mention this is for future reference.
I stumbled on this comment while cleaning up the path code today. Almost 10 years later, and apparently the future reference is still paying rent. :P

> Shouldn't vim_FullName just return FAIL for a failure, as the function comments say?

Sure, maybe. But that's a more involved change. For the particular case here, it seems to me the intention of the existing code is for `FullName_save()` to behave similarly to `vim_FullName()`, which means it should truncate, not return NULL.

By the way: how did you encounter this bug? Do you have steps to reproduce it?

Built with `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCLANG_ASAN_UBSAN=ON ..`

Reproduced by issuing `:Unite grep:.:-Q` in a directory with extremely many big text files.

Heap overflow after this call to `fnamemodify()`:
https://github.com/Shougo/unite.vim/blob/master/autoload/unite/sources/grep.vim#L239

```
call unite#filters#matcher_default#use(['matcher_fuzzy'])
call unite#filters#sorter_default#use(['sorter_rank'])
let g:unite_source_grep_command='ag'
let g:unite_source_grep_default_opts='--nocolor --nogroup'
let g:unite_source_grep_recursive_opt=''
```

I fail to see where the problem is.  When the name is long it is copied to allocated memory as-is.
Do you have a stack trace?  Or a simple Vim script that reproduces the problem?
`call fnamemodify(repeat('a', 4096) . '/a', ':p')`
Perhaps a change localized to `modify_fname()` is needed instead.

If I do this in Vim under valgrind:
call fnamemodify(repeat('a', 4096) . '/a', ':p')
I don't see any problem.  Perhaps this is a neovim problem only?

@justinmk I would not call it a bug in `path_get_absolute_path`, it's being passed an incorrect `len`.

@nfnty Right, but `path_get_absolute_path()` is a private function that `vim_FullName()` expects to do the dirty work and either return OK or FAIL. We can either check the length in `vim_FullName()` or `path_get_absolute_path()`, doesn't matter too much. What does matter is that `FullName_save()` must return FAIL so that `vim_FullName()` reacts appropriately.
Then this should be a better solution.

Posted a possible solution (with a test) here: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/5755

We could use some of the documentation updates from here as well.
Really don't think that you should push the problem to `path_get_absolute_path()`.

> Really don't think that you should push the problem to path_get_absolute_path().

`vim_FullName()` then?
Yes, that's what this PR does now. This PR doesn't change any behavior, only fixes the bug in an explicit way.
Should I merge your test case?
I guess what you're referring to is `vim_FullName()` should return `FAIL` if `path_get_absolute_path()` fails?
But then shouldn't `vim_FullName()` also return `FAIL` if `fname` is truncated, even if `fname` is a URL?

> This PR doesn't change any behavior, only fixes the bug in an explicit way.

It does change the behavior. See https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/5737#discussion_r91868801

Sure.

> I guess what you're referring to is vim_FullName() should return FAIL if path_get_absolute_path() fails?

At least that. More generally, let's make the minimum changes that fix the bug without having to analyze lots of changes, unless those changes are a significant improvement.
